items.prompt: Explain how a National Development Plan can provide direction rather than a list of wishes.
items.canonical_answer: It links priorities to objectives, resources, responsibilities and actions. Monitoring compares results with intended outcomes so implementation can be assessed and adjusted.
marking_guidance: Reason: connect a planning component to coordinated implementation or assessment of outcomes.

items.prompt: Describe how an invented district could use a development-planning cycle to address long journeys that prevent access to training.
items.canonical_answer: Establish the access problem and a measurable objective; choose a feasible route or local-provision response; allocate resources and responsibilities; implement it and compare participation and completion with the baseline, then adjust unresolved barriers.
marking_guidance: Sequence: move coherently from problem/objective through implementation to monitoring and adjustment.
Application: connect the stages to training access and the travel barrier; unrelated generic stages are insufficient.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Differentiate the economic-advancement pillar from the infrastructure-development pillar of the first Harambee Prosperity Plan.
items.canonical_answer: Economic advancement concerns productive opportunities and employment. Infrastructure development concerns supporting networks such as water, electricity and transport.
marking_guidance: Comparison, up to 2 marks: distinguish productive opportunities/employment from supporting physical networks. Give credit for one accurate feature of each pillar, not two repetitions of the same feature.

items.prompt: Explain how to judge NDP5 against its stated goals of inclusive and equitable economic growth, people’s capabilities and health, environmental protection and resilience, and effective governance. A fictional district records more jobs but no rise in reliable water access in remote settlements. Weigh this mixed evidence; it is not a national result.
items.canonical_answer: More jobs can support inclusive and equitable economic growth if the benefit reaches different groups. Unchanged remote water access gives no evidence of improved access to that service and may indicate uneven gains in people’s capabilities and health. These results alone do not establish environmental protection, resilience or effective governance; each needs relevant evidence. Judge the goals separately and avoid claiming overall success from employment alone.
marking_guidance: Judgement: acknowledge partial progress and the inclusion gap.
Reason: connect both supplied observations to named NDP5 goals, distinguish fictional district evidence from a real national verdict.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Describe two features of short-term development planning.
items.canonical_answer: It specifies nearer actions and deadlines. It assigns the resources and responsibilities needed to implement those actions in support of a wider goal.
marking_guidance: Feature: nearer operational actions and concrete resource/responsibility arrangements.

items.prompt: Describe two features of long-term development planning.
items.canonical_answer: It sets a direction and intended outcomes over a longer horizon. It coordinates linked stages, with progress monitored and the route revised where conditions change.
marking_guidance: Feature: longer direction/outcomes and connected stages or capacity to adjust the route.

items.prompt: State (a) the first Harambee Prosperity Plan’s launch year and the president who introduced it [2]. Explain (b) what this fictional evidence implies for the social-progression and infrastructure aims [4]: a funded project completes two water points, but repeated breakdowns leave half the intended households without reliable access.
items.canonical_answer: (a) 2016; President Hage Geingob. (b) Construction contributes to the infrastructure aim, but half the intended households still lack reliable access. That limits the social benefit: an installed point is an output, while dependable usable water is an outcome. Maintenance and evidence on actual reach are needed before judging success against both aims.
marking_guidance: Point (a), 2 marks: accurate year and president.
Development (b), up to 4 marks: link completed infrastructure, breakdowns and unequal reliable access to a bounded judgement about intended outcomes.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.

items.prompt: Describe (a) how three pillars of the first Harambee Prosperity Plan are illustrated by this fictional programme [3]: an audit team publishes spending decisions, apprentices gain productive skills for paid work, and maintained electricity connections serve workshops. Suggest (b) an immediate response where four training centres have opened but only one has regular tutors and attendance has not improved; qualified tutors can be reassigned within the available budget [3].
items.canonical_answer: (a) Effective governance is illustrated by published spending decisions that support accountability. Economic advancement is illustrated by skills for productive paid work. Infrastructure development is illustrated by maintained electricity networks serving workshops. (b) Reassign suitable tutors to the operating centres and publish a reliable timetable, checking their availability and the effect on other centres. This makes existing training space more usable instead of merely increasing building numbers. Monitor attendance and learning access to see whether the delivery barrier has improved.
marking_guidance: Evidence (a), 3 marks: describe three distinct HPP pillars by linking each to its supplied action and contribution. A bare list of labels is insufficient; allow other accurate descriptions supported by the source.
Meaning (b), up to 3 marks: propose a feasible tutor/timetable response, connect it to usable training access and explain how delivery will be checked within the available resources.
Original indicative practice guidance; not an official mark scheme.
